_about: AI-assisted research and compilation with ChatGPT (OpenAI). Entries reflect publicly documented senior figures and stated legal status as of each cited source date. No precise locations or operational route details are included.

sources.title: Seventeen Alleged Leaders and Associates of Clan Usuga Indicted in Brooklyn and Miami
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, U.S. Attorney’s Office, Eastern District of New York
sources.claim: The indictment describes Clan Úsuga as a Colombian drug-trafficking group and names senior leaders charged in international cocaine conspiracies.

sources.title: Former Leader of Clan Del Golfo Drug Trafficking Organization Sentenced to 45 Years in Prison
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, U.S. Attorney’s Office, Eastern District of New York
sources.claim: The court release identifies Clan del Golfo as a major cocaine-trafficking organization and states that Dairo Antonio Úsuga David led it.

sources.title: Leader of Clan Del Golfo Charged in Superseding Indictment
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, U.S. Attorney’s Office, Eastern District of New York
sources.claim: The 2026 filing calls Jobanis de Jesús Ávila Villadiego the principal leader and describes the organization’s continuing cocaine-trafficking activity.

people.name: Dairo Antonio Úsuga David
people.roleLabel: Former principal leader; convicted of leading a continuing criminal enterprise and cocaine-trafficking conspiracies

sources.title: Former Leader of Clan Del Golfo Drug Trafficking Organization Sentenced to 45 Years in Prison
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, U.S. Attorney’s Office, Eastern District of New York
sources.claim: The court states that Úsuga, also known as Otoniel, led Clan del Golfo, pleaded guilty to three charges, and received concurrent 45-year sentences for a continuing criminal enterprise and narcotics conspiracies.

sources.title: Colombian Drug Kingpin and Paramilitary Leader Sentenced to 35 Years in Prison
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, U.S. Attorney’s Office, Eastern District of New York
sources.claim: The court identifies Rendón Herrera, known as Don Mario, as a leader of Clan del Golfo’s predecessor organization and sentences him to 35 years for a continuing criminal enterprise.

sources.title: El Tesoro actúa contra operaciones de tráfico de fentanilo del Cártel de Sinaloa y contra líder de cártel colombiano

sources.claim: OFAC designated Ávila, alias Chiquito Malo, identifying him as Clan del Golfo’s leader and saying the group supplied cocaine to major trafficking organizations.
